title: A Promotion Conversation I Had to Rehearse
script: Narrator: [nervously] I postponed asking about promotion for four months. My manager often praised my work, but praise did not explain what the next role required, and I worried that raising the subject would sound entitled.

Narrator: I prepared by reviewing the published role description. I listed projects I had led, measurable results, and responsibilities I was already handling. I also noted gaps, including a budgeting skill I had not yet demonstrated.

Narrator: [carefully] Before the meeting, a mentor helped me replace vague claims with questions. Instead of saying, “I deserve more,” I planned to ask, “Which criteria am I meeting, which am I not, and what evidence would show readiness?”

Narrator: The conversation was less dramatic than I feared. My manager agreed that my client work matched the next level but said I lacked experience supervising a full project budget. She could not promise a promotion date because the department's hiring plan was unsettled.

Narrator: [thoughtful] We created a six-month development plan with two budget tasks, monthly feedback, and a formal review date. I asked for the agreement in writing so that both of us would remember the same commitments.
Narrator: I also asked how salary bands were set and who approved changes. The answers were not perfect, but they made the process more visible.

Narrator: [honestly] A development plan is not a guarantee. Business conditions can change, and meeting criteria should lead to a fair review, not an automatic promise that no manager is authorised to make.
Narrator: I left without a new title, yet with something useful: specific evidence to build and a date when the decision could no longer be postponed through general compliments.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator delay asking about promotion for four months?
options: She feared the question would sound entitled.
General praise hides differences in individual contributions.
She regularly made her contributions visible to leadership.
Professional feedback feels like a betrayal of their friendship.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: She feared the question would sound entitled.

quiz.question: Why was general praise insufficient preparation for advancement?
options: The most visible person may receive credit for quieter work.
It did not define the requirements of the next role.
Reliable within the team but nearly invisible beyond it.
He cannot correct a problem nobody states clearly.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It did not define the requirements of the next role.

quiz.question: What evidence did the narrator gather before meeting the manager?
options: Documented contributions should matter more than popularity.
The narrator confused useful visibility with vanity.
Projects, measurable results, and current responsibilities.
Discuss deadlines professionally while keeping friendship outside that conversation.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Projects, measurable results, and current responsibilities.

quiz.question: Which readiness gap did the narrator identify personally?
options: Collaborative results may depend on several people's work.
The feedback became specific rather than vague.
The team may reasonably doubt whether standards are applied fairly.
She lacked demonstrated experience managing a full budget.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: She lacked demonstrated experience managing a full budget.

quiz.question: How did a mentor improve the planned promotion conversation?
options: Vague claims became questions about criteria and evidence.
Some contributions should be acknowledged privately with consent.
Unseen work cannot always influence decisions, even when it is excellent.
Use specific missed deadlines rather than personal feelings.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Vague claims became questions about criteria and evidence.

quiz.question: Why could the manager not promise a promotion date?
options: An employee says a colleague presented her idea without credit.
The department's future hiring plan remained unsettled.
She regularly made her contributions visible to leadership.
Professional feedback feels like a betrayal of their friendship.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The department's future hiring plan remained unsettled.

quiz.question: What made the six-month plan measurable?
options: Evidence is needed before confirming wrongdoing or assuming jealousy.
Reliable within the team but nearly invisible beyond it.
It included budget tasks, monthly feedback, and a review date.
He cannot correct a problem nobody states clearly.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It included budget tasks, monthly feedback, and a review date.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator request the agreement in writing?
options: Name the action and responsibility without defining the person's character.
The narrator confused useful visibility with vanity.
Discuss deadlines professionally while keeping friendship outside that conversation.
Both people would retain the same record of commitments.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Both people would retain the same record of commitments.

quiz.question: What limitation applies even after every development task is completed?
options: A fair review is due, but promotion is not guaranteed.
Document decisions, ideas, and owners while work is happening.
The feedback became specific rather than vague.
The team may reasonably doubt whether standards are applied fairly.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: A fair review is due, but promotion is not guaranteed.

quiz.question: What useful outcome replaced an immediate new title?
options: Recognition affects promotion, pay, and access to future assignments.
The narrator gained clear evidence targets and a decision date.
Unseen work cannot always influence decisions, even when it is excellent.
Use specific missed deadlines rather than personal feelings.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The narrator gained clear evidence targets and a decision date.
